document_title: Revising Qualified Domestic Trust Regulations Under Section 2056A To Update Outdated References and Procedures

claims.quote: Section 2056A(a) defines the term ``qualified domestic trust,'' with respect to any decedent, as any trust if (1) its trust instrument meets certain requirements regarding the identity and powers of the trustee, (2) such trust meets such requirements as the Secretary may by regulations prescribe to ensure the collection of any tax imposed by section 2056A(b), and (3) an election under section 2056A by the executor of the decedent applies to such trust.
claims.summary: A qualified domestic trust (QDOT) must meet certain requirements regarding the identity and powers of the trustee, meet requirements prescribed by the Secretary to ensure the collection of any tax imposed by section 2056A(b), and have an election under section 2056A by the executor of the decedent apply to it.

claims.quote: Section 2056A(b) generally prescribes rules relating to a deferred estate tax on distributions of corpus from the QDOT during the spouse's lifetime and on the balance of the corpus held in the QDOT at the spouse's death (section 2056A estate tax).
claims.summary: A deferred estate tax is imposed on distributions of corpus from the QDOT during the spouse's lifetime and on the balance of the corpus held in the QDOT at the spouse's death.

claims.quote: Section 2056A(e) directs the Secretary to prescribe regulations as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of section 2056A.
claims.summary: The Secretary is directed to prescribe regulations as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of section 2056A.

claims.quote: Sec.  20.2056A-11 of the 1993 proposed regulations set forth the proposed rules relating to filing requirements and payment of the section 2056A estate tax.
claims.summary: There are filing requirements and payment obligations for the section 2056A estate tax.

claims.quote: The text of the 1995 temporary regulations also served, by cross-reference, as the text of reissued proposed regulations published on the same date in the Federal Register (60 FR 43574) to address and solicit further commentary on the additional requirements necessary to ensure collection of the section 2056A estate tax (1995 proposed regulations).
claims.summary: Additional requirements necessary to ensure collection of the section 2056A estate tax were addressed and solicited for further commentary.

claims.quote: On November 29, 1996, the Treasury Department and the IRS published TD 8686 in the Federal Register (61 FR 60551) to adopt Sec.  20.2056A-2(d) of the 1995 proposed regulations, with modifications in response to comments, as final regulations (1996 final regulations).
claims.summary: The Treasury Department and the IRS adopted Sec. 20.2056A-2(d) of the 1995 proposed regulations, with modifications in response to comments, as final regulations.

claims.quote: the Treasury Department and the IRS adopt two non-substantive changes to these regulations. First, identification of the office known as the ``Estate Tax Advisory Group'' throughout these regulations is clarified to include any successor office as provided in IRS publications, forms or instructions, or on https://www.irs,irs.gov. In the event of a restructuring of the IRS, this will allow the IRS to efficiently and quickly publicize the identity of the successor office, improving clarity for taxpayers. Second, the applicability date is changed so that these regulations will apply on and after the regulations are published as final in the Federal Register, instead of applying only to estates of decedents dying on or after the regulations are published as final in the Federal Register. Because these regulations correct outdated references and procedures, this change will reduce confusion and ensure all taxpayers are able to utilize the updated references and procedures from the time of publication of these regulations in the Federal Register.
claims.summary: Taxpayers must utilize the updated references and procedures from the time of publication of the regulations in the Federal Register.

claims.quote: The Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520) (PRA) requires that a Federal agency obtain the approval of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) before collecting information from the public, whether such collection of information is mandatory, voluntary, or required to obtain or retain a benefit. A Federal agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless the collection of information displays a valid control number.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must obtain OMB approval before collecting information from the public, and a collection of information is not valid unless it displays a valid control number.

claims.quote: The final regulations include third-party disclosure and reporting requirements under Sec.  20.2056A-2(d)(1)(i) for surety and banks to notify trustees and the IRS of the failure to renew a bond or letter of credit.
claims.summary: Surety and banks must notify trustees and the IRS of the failure to renew a bond or letter of credit.

claims.quote: The final regulations include reporting requirements related to a security instrument used to meet the qualifications of a QDOT and filed at the time the executor of an estate files a Form 706 or 706-NA.
claims.summary: The executor of an estate must file a security instrument used to meet the qualifications of a QDOT when filing Form 706 or 706-NA.

claims.quote: The final regulations also include reporting requirements related to Form 706-QDT used to calculate and report the section 2056A estate tax due or to notify the IRS that the trust is exempt from future filing because a noncitizen spouse has become a citizen.
claims.summary: A trust must use Form 706-QDT to calculate and report the section 2056A estate tax due or notify the IRS that the trust is exempt from future filing because a noncitizen spouse has become a citizen.

claims.quote: The final regulations include reporting requirements related to requesting extensions using Form 4768 to file Form 706-QDT, Form 706, and Form 706-NA.
claims.summary: Filers must use Form 4768 to request extensions for filing Form 706-QDT, Form 706, and Form 706-NA.

claims.quote: Books and records relating to a collection of information must be retained as long as their contents might become material in the administration of any internal revenue law.
claims.summary: Books and records relating to a collection of information must be retained as long as their contents might become material in the administration of any internal revenue law.

claims.quote: it is hereby certified that the final regulations will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
claims.summary: The final regulations will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

claims.quote: This rule primarily affects individuals (or their estates) and trusts, which are not small entities for purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
claims.summary: The rule primarily affects individuals, their estates, and trusts, which are not considered small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

claims.quote: Although it is anticipated that there may be an incremental economic impact on executors that are small entities, including entities that provide tax and legal services that assist individuals in preparing tax returns, any impact will not be significant and will not affect a substantial number of small entities.
claims.summary: There may be an incremental economic impact on small entities that are executors, but the impact is not significant and does not affect a substantial number of small entities.

claims.quote: Pursuant to section 7805(f) of the Code, this regulation has been submitted to the Chief Counsel for the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration for comment on its impact on small business.
claims.summary: This regulation has been submitted to the Chief Counsel for the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration for comment on its impact on small business.

claims.quote: Section 202 of the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (UMRA) requires that agencies assess anticipated costs and benefits and take certain other actions before issuing a final rule that includes any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures in any one year by a State, local, or Tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector, of $100 million in 1995 dollars, updated annually for inflation.
claims.affected_party: State, local, Tribal governments, private sector
claims.summary: Agencies must assess anticipated costs and benefits and take certain actions before issuing a final rule that includes any Federal mandate resulting in expenditures of $100 million or more in 1995 dollars, updated annually for inflation.

claims.quote: This rule does not include any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures by State, local, or Tribal governments, or by the private sector in excess of that threshold.
claims.affected_party: State, local, Tribal governments, private sector
claims.summary: This rule does not include any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures exceeding the $100 million threshold.

claims.quote: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) prohibits an agency from publishing any rule that has federalism implications if the rule either imposes substantial, direct compliance costs on State and local governments and is not required by statute, or preempts State law unless the agency meets the consultation and funding requirements of section 6 of the executive order.
claims.summary: An agency is prohibited from publishing a rule with federalism implications unless it meets consultation and funding requirements or the rule does not impose substantial, direct compliance costs on State and local governments or preempt State law.

claims.quote: These final regulations do not have federalism implications and do not impose substantial direct compliance costs on State and local governments or preempt State law within the meaning of the executive order.
claims.summary: The final regulations do not have federalism implications and do not impose substantial direct compliance costs on State and local governments or preempt State law.

claims.quote: The fair market value of assets is the fair market value of those assets as finally determined for Federal estate tax purposes. That value is-- (1) The value reported on an estate tax return filed with the Internal Revenue Service, once the period of limitations on assessment (see section 6501) of estate tax has expired without that value having been timely adjusted by the Internal Revenue Service;
claims.summary: The fair market value of assets is the value reported on an estate tax return filed with the Internal Revenue Service once the period of limitations on assessment of estate tax has expired without that value having been timely adjusted by the Internal Revenue Service.

claims.quote: The value determined or specified by the Internal Revenue Service for unreported property, or for reported property where the value determined or specified by the Internal Revenue Service differs from the value reported on an estate tax return filed with the Internal Revenue Service, once the period of limitations on assessment applicable to the estate tax has expired without that value having been timely contested by the executor;
claims.summary: The value determined or specified by the Internal Revenue Service for unreported property, or for reported property where the value differs, must be used once the period of limitations on assessment applicable to the estate tax has expired without that value having been timely contested by the executor.

claims.quote: The value determined in a written agreement with the Internal Revenue Service (whether entered into during the course of the administrative proceedings between the estate and the Internal Revenue Service or after the commencement of litigation) once that written agreement has been executed by both the executor and the Internal Revenue Service and is binding on all parties (including, but not limited to, the executor, the Internal Revenue Service, and the beneficiaries); or
claims.summary: The value determined in a written agreement with the Internal Revenue Service must be used once that written agreement has been executed by both the executor and the Internal Revenue Service and is binding on all parties.

claims.quote: The value determined by a court for the purpose of determining the estate tax liability of the estate, once the court's determination no longer can be appealed to any court.
claims.summary: The value determined by a court for the purpose of determining the estate tax liability of the estate must be used once the court's determination no longer can be appealed to any court.

claims.quote: The term contested means to put at issue the value of property in a written communication to the Internal Revenue Service that identifies the specific property, states that the executor does not accept as correct the value of that property as determined or specified by the Internal Revenue Service, and provides the executor's claimed value for that property as determined in accordance with the requirements of section 2031, the corresponding regulations, and other applicable guidance. An issue cannot be contested by a general protective statement or written communication that does not include each of these specified elements.
claims.summary: To contest the value of property, the executor must submit a written communication to the Internal Revenue Service that identifies the specific property, states that the executor does not accept the value as determined or specified by the Internal Revenue Service, and provides the executor's claimed value for that property as determined in accordance with the requirements of section 2031, the corresponding regulations, and other applicable guidance.

claims.quote: The term executor includes any person described in section 2203, as expanded to include all persons required under section 6018(b) to file an estate tax return.
claims.summary: The term executor includes any person described in section 2203, as expanded to include all persons required under section 6018(b) to file an estate tax return.

claims.quote: This section applies on and after July 10, 2026.
claims.summary: This section applies on and after July 10, 2026.

claims.quote: I [name] hereby agree that I will report all annuity payments received under the [name of plan or arrangement] on Form 706-QDT for the calendar year and remit, on an annual basis, to the Internal Revenue Service the estate tax that is imposed under section 2056A(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code on the corpus portion of each annuity payment (as defined in Sec.  20.2056A-4(c)(4) of the Estate Tax Regulations) received under the plan during the calendar year.
claims.summary: The surviving spouse must report all annuity payments received under the plan on Form 706-QDT for the calendar year and remit, on an annual basis, to the Internal Revenue Service the estate tax that is imposed under section 2056A(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code on the corpus portion of each annuity payment.

claims.quote: I further agree that if I fail to timely file Form 706-QDT or to timely pay the tax imposed on the corpus portion of any annuity payment (determined after any extensions of time to pay granted to me under the provisions of Sec.  20.2056A-11), I may become immediately liable to pay the amount of the tax determined by application of section 2056A(b)(1) on the entire remaining present value of the annuity, calculated as of the beginning of the year in which the payment was received with respect to which I failed to timely pay the tax or failed to timely file the return.
claims.summary: The surviving spouse may become immediately liable to pay the amount of the tax determined by application of section 2056A(b)(1) on the entire remaining present value of the annuity, calculated as of the beginning of the year in which the payment was received with respect to which the surviving spouse failed to timely pay the tax or failed to timely file the return.

claims.quote: I [name] hereby agree that within 60 days of receipt of each annuity payment paid under [name of plan or arrangement], I will transfer an amount equal to percent (the corpus portion determined under Sec.  20.2056A-4(c)(4) of the Estate Tax Regulations) of each annuity payment to [identify the QDOT].
claims.summary: The surviving spouse must transfer the corpus portion of each annuity payment to the QDOT within 60 days of receipt.

claims.quote: I will report all annuity payments received during the calendar year under the [name of plan or arrangement] on Form 706-QDT including a schedule of transfers to the [identify the QDOT].
claims.summary: The surviving spouse must report all annuity payments received during the calendar year on Form 706-QDT, including a schedule of transfers to the QDOT.

claims.quote: I also agree that Form 706-QDT is to be filed no later than April 15th of the year following the year in which any annuity payments are received except that: in the case of annuity payments received in the year of my spouse's death, Form 706-QDT shall not be due prior to the due date, including extensions, for filing my spouse's estate tax return, or, if no return is filed, no later than 9 months from the date of my spouse's death (except if I am granted an extension of time to file Form 706-QDT under the provisions of Sec.  20.2056A-11); and in the year of my death, the Form 706-QDT must be filed no later than the date my estate tax return is filed (or if no return is filed, no later than 9 months from the date of my death), and except if I am granted an extension of time to file Form 706-QDT under the provisions of Sec.  20.2056A-11.
claims.summary: Form 706-QDT must be filed by the surviving spouse no later than April 15th of the year following the year in which any annuity payments are received, with exceptions for annuity payments received in the year of the spouse's death or the year of the surviving spouse's death.

claims.quote: I further agree that if I fail to timely transfer any required amount with respect to any annuity payment, or fail to timely file Form 706-QDT reporting the transfers for any year, I may become immediately liable to pay the amount of the tax determined by application of section 2056A(b)(1) on the entire remaining present value of the annuity, calculated as of the beginning of the year in which the payment was received with respect to which I failed to make the timely transfer or timely file a return.
claims.summary: Failure to timely transfer the corpus portion of any annuity payment or to timely file Form 706-QDT may result in immediate liability to pay the tax on the entire remaining present value of the annuity.

claims.quote: However, I may make an application for relief under Sec.  301.9100-1 of the Procedure and Administration Regulations, from the consequences of failing to timely file Form 706-QDT or failing to timely transfer the corpus portion of any annuity payment to the QDOT.
claims.summary: The surviving spouse may apply for relief under Sec. 301.9100-1 for failing to timely file Form 706-QDT or to timely transfer the corpus portion of any annuity payment to the QDOT.

An extension of time beyond the due date to pay any part of the estate tax imposed on lifetime distributions under section 2056A(b)(1)(A), or imposed at the death of the surviving spouse under section 2056A(b)(1)(B), or imposed at the termination of the QDOT (such as on the death or resignation of the U.S. trustee), may be granted for a reasonable period of time, not to exceed 6 months (12 months in the case of the estate tax imposed under section 2056A(b)(1)(B) at the surviving spouse's death), by the Advisory Group Managers (or their delegate or designee or as otherwise provided in IRS publications, forms or instructions, or on https://www.irs.gov).
